messages.text: Sainz signs multi-year contract extension with Williams

metadata.summary: Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams that will keep him with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season and beyond.
metadata.content: Carlos Sainz: Williams driver signs multi-year contract extension to remain with team for 2027 F1 season and beyond | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Carlos Sainz: Williams driver signs multi-year contract extension to remain with team for 2027 F1 season and beyond Carlos Sainz signs multi-year extension with Williams; announcement follows team-mate Alex Albon signing extension a day earlier; watch the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint weekend live on Sky Sports F1 from Friday Wednesday 19 August 2026 14:53, UK Image: Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams Carlos Sainz has signed a multi-year contract extension with Williams that will keep him with the team for the 2027 Formula 1 season and beyond. The 31-year-old Spaniard had expressed doubt over his future with Williams amid a second campaign with the team that has failed to deliver the strong results of 2025, which makes his decision to sign a multi-year deal something of a surprise. Wednesday's announcement came a day after the team confirmed Sainz's team-mate Alex Albon had signed a one-year extension to remain with the team for the 2027 season, with both drivers' previous deals having been set to expire at the end of 2026. messages.text: Hull KR sweating on Lewis after sin-binning on return from four-match ban

metadata.summary: After returning from a four-game ban, Mikey Lewis is now sweating on whether he will miss more crucial matches in Hull KR's run-in.
metadata.content: Mikey Lewis: Hull KR left sweating as star man sent to sin bin against Warrington Wolves on return from four-match ban | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to content Mikey Lewis: Hull KR left sweating as star man sent to sin bin against Warrington Wolves on return from four-match ban Mikey Lewis was sent to the sin bin for Hull KR on his return from a four-match ban; The yellow card was for dangerous contact with kicker Ewan Irwin as his studs hit his ankle; Hull KR sit fifth with four games remaining in the regular season Megan Wellens Sports Journalist @MegWellensX Wednesday 19 August 2026 12:57, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mikey Lewis is given his fourth yellow card of the season in his first game back from a four-match suspension. After returning from a four-game ban, Mikey Lewis is now sweating on whether he will miss more crucial matches in Hull KR's run-in. Lewis was banned for a headbutt during the Robins' away loss to Warrington and during that period, his side won all four matches without their star halfback. It was wondered whether Hull KR would stick with Ryan Hampshire due to their winning run but Peters opted to bring Lewis back in, citing the learning curve he has been on over the last month.
